The petitioner filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by him in a road traffic accident.

sentences.text:
The brief facts of the petitioner's case are as under:
2. That on 17.8.2023 at about 9.30 p.m. the petitioner was walking on the left side of Kanakapura main road, Banashankari Signal junction, Jayanagar 8th Block,
Bengaluru along with one Sunil H.L., at that time, driver of BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-4997 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.
Due to said impact, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately he was shifted to Victoria Hospital, Bengaluru,
wherein he took treatment as an inpatient and by spending Rs.2,00,000/- towards medical expenses, conveyance and nourishment food etc.,
3.

It is stated that prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 30 years and working as a driver and also doing agriculture and earning 40,000/- p.m. and contributing the same towards maintenance of his family.
Due to accidental injuries, he could not able to his activities as earlier.
4. It is stated that, the accident occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-4997.
Hence, the Jayanagar Traffic Police have registered criminal case against driver of the offending vehicle in Crime No.343/2023 for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC.
As such, the respondent is liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner has filed the instant petition, seeking compensation.
5. In response to the notice, the respondent appeared through its counsel and filed the written statement.
6. In the written statement of the respondent has contended that the petition is not maintainable either in law or on facts.

Further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner as the bus was on its schedule trip from Hebbal to Bhanashankari, when he reached Bhanashankari bus stand, the driver in order to enter the bus stand and taking left turn, the petitioner in order to cross the main road, darted the path of the bus and exposed himself for the alleged accident.
Further denied the age, avocation and income of the petitioner.
Ultimately stated that the claim of the petitioner is highly excessive, exaggerated and arbitrary.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition with cost.
7. On the basis of rival pleadings of both the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
ISSUES 1.

Whether the petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a motor vehicle accident which was taken place on 17.8.2023 at about 9.15 p.m. on Kanakapura main road, Banashankari Signal Junction, Jayanagar 6th Block,
Benglauru due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Bus bearing Krishna H M Alias Krishna vs B.M.T.C on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8491726/
2 registration No.KA-57-F-4997 in an actionable negligence?
2. Whether petitioner is entitled for compensation?

Apart from his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.B.Ramesh as PW2 and got marked the documents at Ex.P11 to Ex.P13.
9.

On the other hand, the respondent got examined its driver as RW1 and got marked documents as Ex.R1 to Ex.R4.
10.
Heard the arguments of both the counsel and perused the materials available on record.

11. My answer to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per final order,

 R E A S O N S ISSUE NO.1:-
12.

It is the specific case of the petitioner that due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA- 57-F-4997, the alleged accident had taken place, consequently he had sustained grievous injuries.

13. On the contrary, the respondent though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner, but strongly disputed the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC bus.
In such a situation, burden is more on the part of the petitioner, to prove the above issues on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
14. The petitioner in order to prove his case, petitioner examined himself as PW1.
In his examination-in-chief by way of affidavit has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
PW1 in support of his oral evidence has relied upon Ex.
P1 to Ex.P5
. Ex.P1-true copy of the F.I.R. in Crime No.343/2023 of Jayanagar Traffic Police Station.

Ex.P2- true copy of first information statement given by one Sunila, Ex.P3-true copy charge sheet, Ex.P4- true copy of wound certificate, Ex.P5-true Krishna H M Alias Krishna vs B.M.T.C on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8491726/

15. On perusal of the police documents, it could be seen that, based upon the first information statement given by one Sunila, the S.H.O. of Jayanagar Traffic police has registered the case against the driver of the offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Sections 279 and 337 of I.P.C.

Upon investigation, the I.O. has filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle alleging that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.
16.
On the contrary, driver of the BMTC bus bearing No.KA-57-F-4997 was examined as RW1.

He has strongly contended that, on the date of accident he was on his schedule trip from Hebbal to Bhanashankari, when he reached Bhanashankari bus stand, in order to enter the bus stand and taking left turn, the petitioner in order to cross the main road, darted the path of the bus and exposed himself for the alleged accident.
Hence, he is no way responsible for the cause of accident.

To prove the defenses of the respondent, no convincing materials available on record for consideration. Even in the cross-examination, no material points are forthcoming to disbelieve the case of the petitioner.

17. Apart from this, at the time of cross- examination of PW1, no material answers culled out to believe the defenses of the respondent about the denial of allegation made against the driver of the offending vehicle.
18. In the light of the evidence placed by petitioner, I am of the view that, the petitioner has placed satisfactory and acceptable evidence to prove the above issue.

Hence, I hold that, the accident was occurred purely on the part of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing No.KA- 57-F-4997 and in the said accident, petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

Accordingly,
I am answering the Issue No.1 is in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.2:
19.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident under different heads.

20. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another of the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India.
"In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.

The object of awarding Krishna H M Alias Krishna vs B.M.T.C on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8491726/
4 compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."

sentences.text: "while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite party saying that nothing is payable.
That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that, he has sustained the injuries in a road traffic accident.
In connection with the injuries he has produced wound certificate marked as Ex.P4.

The said document discloses that, he had sustained the following injuries:-
1) Crush injury of right foot with muscle and tendons exposed with active bleeding.
X-ray of right foot distal and proximal phalanx shows 2nd and 3rd proximal phalanx fracture and 3rd metatarsal fracture.
22. In connection with the above said injuries are grievous in nature.
Further, the petitioner has produced outpatient record, discharge summaries and x-ray as per Ex.P7 to Ex.P9.
On perusal of discharge summary marked at Ex.P8 shows that the petitioenr was admitted from 18.8.2023 to 31.8.2023.
In addition to his evidence placed the evidence of Dr.B.Ramesh as PW2.

He has deposed that the petitioner has sustained crush injury right foot with 1st toe phalanx fracture, 2nd and 3rd fracture of phalanx first toe fracture proximal phalanx second and third toe and fracture of 3 rd metatarsal lisfrance dislocation of foot cuneiform comminuted fracture.

He has placed case sheet,
outpatient record and x-ray at Ex.P11 to Ex.P13.

By taking into consideration of the nature of the injuries and the treatment taken by the petitioner, he could have undergone pain and sufferings while taking treatment, as an in patient as well as an outpatient.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of Pain and Sufferings.
Loss of income during treatment period:
23.
PW1 has stated that, he was working as a driver and also doing agriculture and earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
He has not placed any iota of documents to show his income.
In the absence of the documents, it is apt to be considered notional income of the petitioner.
On going through the discharge summary marked at Ex.P8 shows that the petitioenr was admitted from 18.8.2023 to 31.8.2023.

During the period of treatment, definitely, there was some difficulty to him to do daily routine work and to do his work for livelihood at least for a period of two months by looking in to the nature of the injuries sustained by him.
Hence, I am of the view that, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.32,000/- towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

sentences.text: The petitioner in connection with his treatment expenses produced medical bills at Ex.P10 to the extent of Rs.24,181/- along with prescriptions at Ex.P15.
Except the suggestion there are no contra materials to show that the medical bills are created for the purpose of this case.

Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.24,181/-
towards medical expenses.

Attendant charges, food and nourishment and conveyance charges;
25.

The petitioner herein, as per the medical records and also on going through the discharge summaries the petitioner has taken treatment as an inpatient and as an outpatient, definitely the petitioner could have spent some amount towards, food, nourishment, conveyance, as well as towards attendant charges.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/-
towards attendant charges, food, nourishment and conveyance charges.

Loss of future income;
26.The petitioner herein, asserting that, he had sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by him.
In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on his evidence along with the wound certificate and other medical documents.

In the evidence of the PW1,
reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P4 goes to show that, he had sustained grievous injuries for which he took the treatment as an inpatient.
Apart from this, another material witness by name Dr.B.Ramesh examined as PW2.

PW2 has stated in his evidence that the petitioner has sustained crush injury right foot with 1st toe phalanx fracture, 2nd and 3rd fracture of phalanx first toe fracture proximal phalanx second and third toe and fracture of 3rd metatarsal lisfrance dislocation of foot cuneiform comminuted fracture, for which he underwent wound debridement and fractures treated conservatively.

Further, PW2 has stated that, at the time of his examination of the petitioner on 13.1.2025 petitioner has deformity of right foot, restriction of joint movement of right ankle,
difficulty to squat on floor, climb upstairs walk on slope, sit cross-legged, stand on affected limb.
X-ray shows fracture non-union of III metatarsal other fracture united.
He has assessed the disability 28% of right lower limb and 14% of whole body.
27. At the time of cross-examination of PW2, stated that he is the treated doctor and also denied the suggestion that he assessed the disability of the petitioner on higher side.
28. Over all appreciation of evidence of PW2 along with the entire medical documents the disability expressed by PW2 as 28% of right lower limb and 14% of whole body.

Hence, by taking into consideration of point of disability expressed by PW2, it is apt to take whole body disability as 9%
instead of 14%.
The same will meets the ends of justice.

sentences.text: In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, his age was 30 years.

In support of the age proof,
he has placed Aadhar card marked at Ex.P6 for consideration.

On going through the said document,
the date of birth of the petitioner has been mentioned as 20.5.1993.
The accident occurred on 17.8.2023.
Therefore, as on the date of accident, the age of the petitioner is considered as 30 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '17' is to be taken into consideration.

30. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in his evidence the petitioner has stated that, prior to the accident he was working as a driver and also doing agriculture and getting an income of Rs.40,000/- per month.
He has not produced any iota of document to show his income.
In the absence of the material documents, notional income has to be taken into consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
It is pertinent to note that, in the case on hand, the alleged accident had taken place in the year 2023.

As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.16,000/- for the year 2023.
31.

In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner,
definitely come in the way of his future, in a slight manner, to do his daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood on going through his age criteria.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.16,000 X 12 X 17 X9/100= Rs.2,93,760/-.
Loss of amenities;
32.
PW1 has stated in his evidence that due to the accidental injuries he is unable to stand and unable to do his work as earlier.
On perusal of evidence of PW2 and also medical documents, I am of the view that, the petitioner will suffer a slight problem in future also, to do his normal work, as well as his work for livelihood.

Hence, it is just and proper to award compensation of Rs.15,000/-
towards loss of amenities.

Future Medical Expenses;
33.
PW2 has not stated about the future medication.
Hence, petitioner is not entitled for compensation under the head of future medication.

34. In view of my discussions held above, on various aspects the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
Compensation heads Compensation amount 1.Pain and Suffering Rs. 40,000-00 Krishna H M Alias Krishna vs B.M.T.C on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8491726/
7
2.Loss of income during Rs. 32,000-00 laid-up period and rest period

3. Medical expenses Rs. 24,181-00 4. Attendant, Nourishment Rs. 15,000-00 and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs.2,93,760-00 due to disability 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 15,000-00 7.Future medical expenses NIL Total Rs.4,19,941-00 35.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,19,941/- (Rupees four lakh nineteen thousand nine hundred and forty one only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,
between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated. 20.03.2018.
And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.

LIABILITY:
36.

As regards the liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the BMTC Bus bearing registration No.KA-57-F-4997 alleged accident had taken place.
The evidence given by the petitioner in connection with the issue No.1, remained unshaken.

In such a situation, the respondent being the owner cum internal insurance company of the offending vehicle BMTC bus No.KA- 57-F-4997 is liable to pay the compensation determined by this court to the petitioner along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE No.3:
37.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,19,941/- (Rupees four lakh nineteen thousand nine hundred and forty one only), along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in, MFA No.103557/2016,

And MFA No.30131/2019 dated.12.5.2020, from the date of the petition, till the realization of the award amount.
In such a situation, the respondent being the owner cum internal insurance company of the offending vehicle BMTC bus No.KA- 57-F-4997 is liable to pay the compensation determined by this court to the petitioner along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the petition till its realization.
Accordingly, I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

37.

O R D E R
The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/s 166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with cost.
